**1. PURPOSE**

This charter authorises the Temperature Monitoring Upgrade Project (hereafter TMU-2023) and defines its scope, objectives, key stakeholders, and initial risk posture. The project will replace the existing analogue temperature recording infrastructure across the Eastern Creek and Yennora cold-chain warehouses with a networked digital monitoring system, integrate alarm and reporting functions with the existing WMS (Warehouse Management System), and support the broader CR4-EXP expansion of freezer and chiller capacity.

The project charter for the Temperature Monitoring Upgrade Project records its start_date as 2023-03-01. Record status: current.

---

**2. BACKGROUND AND CONTEXT**

The current temperature monitoring at both sites relies on a mix of chart recorders and manual spot checks. The chart recorders are at end-of-life; replacement chart paper is becoming difficult to source and the calibration service we use has advised it will not support the Eastern Creek units beyond June 2023. In addition, the CR4-EXP program will add approximately 4,500 pallet positions of new freezer and chiller space, which must be covered by the monitoring system from day one of that expansion.

A six-week discovery phase was completed in February 2023 by the engineering services contractor (ESC) under a pre-engagement agreement. That work confirmed the feasibility of a single networked system covering both sites, with a central alarm desk at Eastern Creek and a satellite monitoring point at Yennora. The discovery report (ref: ESC-2023-011) is referenced in the project file and forms the technical basis for this charter.

---

**3. PROJECT OBJECTIVES**

1. **Replace all obsolete chart recorders** at Eastern Creek and Yennora with digital temperature and humidity sensors, with a target of full decommissioning of chart recorders by 30 September 2023.
2. **Implement a centralised monitoring platform** with real-time dashboards, configurable alarm thresholds, and audit-trail logging, accessible to the cold-chain operations team and quality assurance.
3. **Integrate alarm notifications** with the existing on-call paging system and the WMS so that temperature excursions generate a work order automatically.
4. **Provide training** to all shift supervisors and a nominated group of leading hands on the new system, with refresher material made available on the intranet.
5. **Support the CR4-EXP timeline** by having the new monitoring coverage in place for the new freezer and chiller zones before commissioning begins (planned for October 2023, to be confirmed).

---

**4. SCOPE**

- Networking infrastructure within the cold-chain areas, including wireless bridges where physical cabling is not practical.
- Removal and disposal of chart recorders and associated paper archives (subject to records retention requirements – see Section 8).
- User acceptance testing, training, and a 30-day parallel run alongside the existing manual checks.

**4.2 Out of Scope**

**2. INCIDENT REVIEW – COLD ROOM 3 TEMPERATURE EXCURSION (19/11/23)**

**2.1 Summary of event**
L. Chen presented the timeline from the data logger and the WMS alarm log. The excursion occurred during the 06:00–14:00 shift on Sunday 19/11/23. The room set point is 2°C to 4°C. The logger recorded a peak of 7.8°C for a duration of 41 minutes before the alarm was acknowledged and the room returned to set point.

**2.2 Contributing factors (as per investigation)**
- Door left ajar on the loading dock side for approximately 25 minutes during a pallet transfer. The automatic door closer was found to be functioning below specification (closing time measured at 18 seconds; spec is <10 seconds).
- The alarm acknowledgement policy requires a response within 15 minutes. The on-duty technician was attending a compressor fault on Cold Room 1 and did not see the mobile alert for 22 minutes.
- The data log shows the room temperature did not drop below 7.0°C for the full 41 minutes, which triggered the high-temperature alarm but not the critical alarm (set at 8.0°C).

**2.3 Corrective actions (already implemented)**
1. Door closer on Cold Room 3 dock-side door was replaced on 21/11/23. R. Haddad confirmed the closing time is now 6 seconds, measured over 10 cycles.
2. A second mobile alert escalation was added to the alarm configuration. The first alert goes to the duty technician; if not acknowledged within 10 minutes, a second alert goes to the shift manager and the warehouse manager. Change request CR-14 was raised and approved by M. Tran on 22/11/23.
3. A reminder notice about the pallet transfer protocol was posted on the dock-side door and included in the 23/11/23 shift briefings at both sites.

L. Chen reported that the door closer replacement has been monitored for 72 hours and no further excursions have been recorded. 3. DEFINITIONS

- **Cold Chain:** The uninterrupted series of refrigerated production, storage, and distribution activities which maintain a given temperature range.
- **Cold Room:** A temperature-controlled storage area maintained at a specified temperature range.
- **Temperature Excursion:** Any event where the temperature of a cold room or product deviates from the specified acceptable range.
- **ESKY:** Insulated portable container used for short-duration transport of temperature-sensitive product.
- **Ute:** Utility vehicle used for local transport deliveries.

4. RESPONSIBILITIES

4.1 **Quality & Compliance Manager** is responsible for:
- Maintaining this procedure and ensuring it is reviewed at least annually.
- Investigating all temperature excursions and ensuring corrective actions are implemented.

4.2 **Warehouse Operations Manager** is responsible for:
- Ensuring all staff are trained on this procedure before undertaking cold chain duties.
- Ensuring temperature monitoring equipment is calibrated and functioning.

4.3 **All Staff** are responsible for:
- Following the requirements of this procedure.
- Reporting any temperature alarms or suspected excursions immediately to the shift supervisor.

5. TEMPERATURE MONITORING

5.1 **Cold Room Temperature Logging**

Each cold room shall have a calibrated temperature monitoring device (either fixed probe or portable data logger) that records temperature at a minimum interval of 15 minutes. Records shall be retained for a minimum of 2 years.

5.2 **Cold Room Temperature Ranges**

The following temperature ranges apply to all SCCS cold storage areas:

5.3 **Alarm Thresholds**

Alarm thresholds are set to provide early warning of potential temperature excursions. The alarm thresholds for each cold room are specified in the temperature monitoring system configuration.

SCCS-SOP-017 specifies that Cold Room 2 temperature_alarm_threshold is -18 degrees Celsius. Record status: current. This threshold is current and applies to the primary alarm setpoint for Cold Room 2. Any temperature reading at or above -18°C in Cold Room 2 will trigger a visual and audible alarm at the monitoring station.

The alarm thresholds for other cold rooms are:
- Cold Room 1: -18°C
- Cold Room 3: +5°C
- Blast Freezer: -28°C
- Chilled Dispatch Staging Bay: +6°C

5.4 **Monitoring System Checks**

The shift supervisor shall perform a visual check of the temperature monitoring system at the start of each shift, and shall document the check on the Daily Temperature Monitoring Checklist (Form SCCS-F-014). The check shall confirm that:
- The monitoring system is displaying current temperatures for all cold rooms.
- No alarms are active.
- The date and time on the monitoring system are correct.

6. TEMPERATURE ALARM RESPONSE

6.1 **Immediate Response**

When a temperature alarm is activated, the following steps shall be taken:

1. The shift supervisor shall acknowledge the alarm at the monitoring station within 15 minutes of activation.
2. The shift supervisor shall attend the affected cold room to verify the temperature reading with a calibrated handheld probe.
3. If the handheld probe confirms the alarm reading, the shift supervisor shall assess whether product integrity has been compromised.

6.2 **Product Assessment**

If the temperature in a cold room has exceeded the acceptable temperature range for more than 30 minutes, the affected product shall be quarantined and assessed. The assessment shall be documented on the Temperature Excursion Report (Form SCCS-F-016).

6.3 **Escalation**

If the temperature cannot be brought back within the acceptable range within 60 minutes of alarm activation, the Quality & Compliance Manager shall be notified immediately. The Quality & Compliance Manager shall determine whether product disposition is required.

7. RECEIPT OF TEMPERATURE-CONTROLLED PRODUCT

7.1 **Receiving Procedures**

All temperature-controlled product received at the dock shall be:
- Checked for the presence of an accompanying temperature recorder or temperature indicator.
- Inspected visually for signs of damage, thawing, or temperature abuse.
- Moved into the appropriate cold room within 30 minutes of receipt.
- Cold Room 1: -18°C (frozen storage)
- Cold Room 2: -25°C (ice cream / deep frozen)
- Cold Room 3: +5°C (chilled storage)
- Cold Room 4: +2°C (high-care chilled)
- Blast Freezer: -28°C
- Chilled Dispatch Staging Bay: +6°C

5.2 **Temperature Monitoring**

Temperatures shall be monitored continuously by the automated monitoring system. The system shall record temperatures at intervals of no greater than 10 minutes. Records shall be retained for a minimum of 3 years.

5.3 **Manual Temperature Checks**

In addition to the automated system, manual temperature checks shall be performed twice per shift using a calibrated handheld probe. The results of these checks shall be recorded on the Daily Temperature Monitoring Checklist (Form SCCS-F-014). The manual check shall be performed at a point that is representative of the product storage conditions, not adjacent to the door or a cooling unit.

5.4 **Probe Calibration**

Handheld probes shall be calibrated at least monthly. Calibration shall be performed against a certified reference thermometer. The calibration result shall be recorded on the Probe Calibration Log (Form SCCS-F-018). Probes that fail calibration shall be removed from service and tagged for repair or disposal.

**6. RECEIPT OF TEMPERATURE-CONTROLLED PRODUCT**

6.1 **Receiving Procedures**

All temperature-controlled product received at the dock shall be:

- Checked for the presence of an accompanying temperature recorder or temperature indicator.
- Inspected visually for signs of damage, thawing, or temperature abuse.
- Moved into the appropriate cold room within 30 minutes of receipt.

6.2 **Documentation Check**

The Receiving Clerk shall review the supplier's temperature recorder or indicator before accepting the product. If the temperature recorder shows that the product exceeded the acceptable range during transit, the Receiving Clerk shall:

1. Notify the Shift Supervisor.
2. Place the product in quarantine immediately.
3. Complete the Temperature Excursion Report (Form SCCS-F-016) within 24 hours.

6.3 **Wet Stock**

Document control shows that SCCS-SOP-017 version is v4.2. Record status: current.

If product is received wet, or shows evidence of thawing (e.g., carton collapse, staining, or ice crystal formation on the product surface), the product shall be quarantined and assessed by the Quality & Compliance Manager before it is accepted into stock.

**7. STORAGE**

7.1 **Stock Rotation**

All temperature-controlled product shall be stored in accordance with the first-in, first-out (FIFO) principle unless otherwise specified by the customer or the product label. Stock that is received with a shorter remaining shelf life than existing stock shall be placed in front of existing stock.

7.2 **Pallet Placement**

- Pallets shall be placed a minimum of 100 mm away from cold room walls and a minimum of 200 mm below ceiling-mounted evaporator units.
- Pallets shall not be placed on the floor directly beneath evaporator units or air vents.
- Pallets shall not obstruct emergency exits, fire extinguishers, or temperature monitoring sensors.
- A minimum aisle width of 1.2 metres shall be maintained between pallet racks.

7.3 **Storage of Damaged or Leaking Product**

Product that is damaged or leaking shall be removed from the cold room immediately and placed in the designated damaged goods area. The Shift Supervisor shall be notified so that the damage can be assessed and documented.

**8. DISPATCH**

8.1 **Staging**

Product to be dispatched shall be moved from the cold room to the Chilled Dispatch Staging Bay no more than 30 minutes prior to the scheduled loading time. Product shall not be staged in an unrefrigerated area.

8.2 **Loading**

- The loading dock door shall be opened only when the transport vehicle is backed into the dock and the dock seal is engaged.
- The loading dock door shall be closed when loading is interrupted for more than 5 minutes.
- The transport vehicle's refrigeration unit shall be running and verified to be at the correct temperature before loading commences.

11.1 **Preventative Maintenance**

All refrigeration units, temperature monitoring equipment, and dock seals shall be maintained in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendations and the Preventative Maintenance Schedule (Form M-101).

11.2 **Calibration**

Temperature monitoring equipment shall be calibrated annually or when the unit has been dropped, damaged, or suspected of being inaccurate. Calibration shall be traceable to a national standard.

14.2 **Induction Training**

New starters shall complete the following modules as part of their induction, before commencing work in the cold chain area:

- Introduction to cold chain principles (including the importance of maintaining temperature integrity)
- Reading and understanding temperature logs

- The probe used for each reading was calibrated and in date

**TEMPERATURE MONITORING UPGRADE PROJECT (TMU-2023)**
**PROJECT CHARTER – REVISION 1.0 (9 MARCH 2023)**

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Project Code | TMU-2023 |
| Related Program | Cold Chain Reliability 4 Expansion (CR4-EXP) |
| Document Owner | Daniel Okafor, Project Manager |
| Revision Date | 9 March 2023 (Rev 1.0 – approved) |
| Next Review | 6 April 2023 |

---

**1. PURPOSE**

This charter authorises the Temperature Monitoring Upgrade Project (hereafter TMU-2023) and defines its scope, objectives, key stakeholders, and initial risk posture. The project will replace the existing analogue temperature recording infrastructure across the Eastern Creek and Yennora cold-chain warehouses with a networked digital monitoring system, integrate alarm and reporting functions with the existing WMS (Warehouse Management System), and support the broader CR4-EXP expansion of freezer and chiller capacity.

The project charter for the Temperature Monitoring Upgrade Project records its start_date as 2023-03-01. Record status: current.

---

**2. BACKGROUND AND CONTEXT**

The current temperature monitoring at both sites relies on a mix of chart recorders and manual spot checks. The chart recorders are at end-of-life; replacement chart paper is becoming difficult to source and the calibration service we use has advised it will not support the Eastern Creek units beyond June 2023. In addition, the CR4-EXP program will add approximately 4,500 pallet positions of new freezer and chiller space, which must be covered by the monitoring system from day one of that expansion.

A six-week discovery phase was completed in February 2023 by the engineering services contractor (ESC) under a pre-engagement agreement. That work confirmed the feasibility of a single networked system covering both sites, with a central alarm desk at Eastern Creek and a satellite monitoring point at Yennora. The discovery report (ref: ESC-2023-011) is referenced in the project file and forms the technical basis for this charter.

---

**3. PROJECT OBJECTIVES**

1. **Replace all obsolete chart recorders** at Eastern Creek and Yennora with digital temperature and humidity sensors, with a target of full decommissioning of chart recorders by 30 September 2023.
2. **Implement a centralised monitoring platform** with real-time dashboards, configurable alarm thresholds, and audit-trail logging, accessible to the cold-chain operations team and quality assurance.
3. **Integrate alarm notifications** with the existing on-call paging system and the WMS so that temperature excursions generate a work order automatically.
4. **Provide training** to all shift supervisors and a nominated group of leading hands on the new system, with refresher material made available on the intranet.
5. **Support the CR4-EXP timeline** by having the new monitoring coverage in place for the new freezer and chiller zones before commissioning begins (planned for October 2023, to be confirmed).

---

**4. SCOPE**

**4.1 In Scope**

- Supply and installation of approximately 340 digital sensor points across both sites (Eastern Creek: 210; Yennora: 130).
- Replacement of the existing alarm panel at Eastern Creek with a new central monitoring server and redundant network switches.
- Configuration of the monitoring software, including alarm set points, notification routing, and reporting templates.
- Networking infrastructure within the cold-chain areas, including wireless bridges where physical cabling is not practical.
- Removal and disposal of chart recorders and associated paper archives (subject to records retention requirements – see Section 8).
- User acceptance testing, training, and a 30-day parallel run alongside the existing manual checks.

**4.2 Out of Scope**

- Changes to the refrigeration plant itself (handled under separate work orders from the maintenance team).
- Calibration of the existing sensors that are being retained (only new sensors are calibrated as part of this project).
- Any works at the third-party cold store at Villawood, which operates under a separate service agreement.
- Software development beyond configuration of the chosen commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) platform.

**2. PROJECT BACKGROUND & OBJECTIVES**

- Incomplete data capture during power outages (no battery backup on loggers)
- No automated alerting for temperature excursions
- Inability to generate audit reports without manual data manipulation
- Calibration records not linked to individual sensors

1. Install a networked sensor array covering all cold rooms, chillers, and freezer areas at both sites
2. Deploy a cloud-based monitoring platform with real-time dashboard and SMS/email alerting
3. Integrate with the existing WMS (SAP EWM) to enable automated stock holds on temperature excursion
4. Provide training and documentation to all relevant staff
5. Achieve full compliance with QA-014 and external audit requirements

documents.title: Standard Operating Procedure SCCS-SOP-017 – Cold Chain Handling
documents.content:
3. DEFINITIONS

- **Cold Chain:** The uninterrupted series of refrigerated production, storage, and distribution activities which maintain a given temperature range.
- **Cold Room:** A temperature-controlled storage area maintained at a specified temperature range.
- **Temperature Excursion:** Any event where the temperature of a cold room or product deviates from the specified acceptable range.
- **ESKY:** Insulated portable container used for short-duration transport of temperature-sensitive product.
- **Ute:** Utility vehicle used for local transport deliveries.

4. RESPONSIBILITIES

4.1 **Quality & Compliance Manager** is responsible for:
- Maintaining this procedure and ensuring it is reviewed at least annually.
- Investigating all temperature excursions and ensuring corrective actions are implemented.

4.2 **Warehouse Operations Manager** is responsible for:
- Ensuring all staff are trained on this procedure before undertaking cold chain duties.
- Ensuring temperature monitoring equipment is calibrated and functioning.

4.3 **All Staff** are responsible for:
- Following the requirements of this procedure.
- Reporting any temperature alarms or suspected excursions immediately to the shift supervisor.

5. TEMPERATURE MONITORING

5.1 **Cold Room Temperature Logging**

Each cold room shall have a calibrated temperature monitoring device (either fixed probe or portable data logger) that records temperature at a minimum interval of 15 minutes. Records shall be retained for a minimum of 2 years.

5.2 **Cold Room Temperature Ranges**

The following temperature ranges apply to all SCCS cold storage areas:

5.3 **Alarm Thresholds**

Alarm thresholds are set to provide early warning of potential temperature excursions. The alarm thresholds for each cold room are specified in the temperature monitoring system configuration.

SCCS-SOP-017 specifies that Cold Room 2 temperature_alarm_threshold is -18 degrees Celsius. Record status: current. This threshold is current and applies to the primary alarm setpoint for Cold Room 2. Any temperature reading at or above -18°C in Cold Room 2 will trigger a visual and audible alarm at the monitoring station.

The alarm thresholds for other cold rooms are:
- Cold Room 1: -18°C
- Cold Room 3: +5°C
- Blast Freezer: -28°C
- Chilled Dispatch Staging Bay: +6°C

5.4 **Monitoring System Checks**

The shift supervisor shall perform a visual check of the temperature monitoring system at the start of each shift, and shall document the check on the Daily Temperature Monitoring Checklist (Form SCCS-F-014). The check shall confirm that:
- The monitoring system is displaying current temperatures for all cold rooms.
- No alarms are active.
- The date and time on the monitoring system are correct.

6. TEMPERATURE ALARM RESPONSE

6.1 **Immediate Response**

When a temperature alarm is activated, the following steps shall be taken:

1. The shift supervisor shall acknowledge the alarm at the monitoring station within 15 minutes of activation.
2. The shift supervisor shall attend the affected cold room to verify the temperature reading with a calibrated handheld probe.
3. If the handheld probe confirms the alarm reading, the shift supervisor shall assess whether product integrity has been compromised.

6.2 **Product Assessment**

If the temperature in a cold room has exceeded the acceptable temperature range for more than 30 minutes, the affected product shall be quarantined and assessed. The assessment shall be documented on the Temperature Excursion Report (Form SCCS-F-016).

6.3 **Escalation**

If the temperature cannot be brought back within the acceptable range within 60 minutes of alarm activation, the Quality & Compliance Manager shall be notified immediately. The Quality & Compliance Manager shall determine whether product disposition is required.

7. RECEIPT OF TEMPERATURE-CONTROLLED PRODUCT

7.1 **Receiving Procedures**

All temperature-controlled product received at the dock shall be:
- Checked for the presence of an accompanying temperature recorder or temperature indicator.
- Inspected visually for signs of damage, thawing, or temperature abuse.
- Moved into the appropriate cold room within 30 minutes of receipt.

documents.title: Standard Operating Procedure SCCS-SOP-017 – Cold Chain Handling
documents.content:
- Cold Room 1: -18°C (frozen storage)
- Cold Room 2: -25°C (ice cream / deep frozen)
- Cold Room 3: +5°C (chilled storage)
- Cold Room 4: +2°C (high-care chilled)
- Blast Freezer: -28°C
- Chilled Dispatch Staging Bay: +6°C

5.2 **Temperature Monitoring**

Temperatures shall be monitored continuously by the automated monitoring system. The system shall record temperatures at intervals of no greater than 10 minutes. Records shall be retained for a minimum of 3 years.

5.3 **Manual Temperature Checks**

In addition to the automated system, manual temperature checks shall be performed twice per shift using a calibrated handheld probe. The results of these checks shall be recorded on the Daily Temperature Monitoring Checklist (Form SCCS-F-014). The manual check shall be performed at a point that is representative of the product storage conditions, not adjacent to the door or a cooling unit.

5.4 **Probe Calibration**

Handheld probes shall be calibrated at least monthly. Calibration shall be performed against a certified reference thermometer. The calibration result shall be recorded on the Probe Calibration Log (Form SCCS-F-018). Probes that fail calibration shall be removed from service and tagged for repair or disposal.

**6. RECEIPT OF TEMPERATURE-CONTROLLED PRODUCT**

6.1 **Receiving Procedures**

All temperature-controlled product received at the dock shall be:

- Checked for the presence of an accompanying temperature recorder or temperature indicator.
- Inspected visually for signs of damage, thawing, or temperature abuse.
- Moved into the appropriate cold room within 30 minutes of receipt.

6.2 **Documentation Check**

The Receiving Clerk shall review the supplier's temperature recorder or indicator before accepting the product. If the temperature recorder shows that the product exceeded the acceptable range during transit, the Receiving Clerk shall:

1. Notify the Shift Supervisor.
2. Place the product in quarantine immediately.
3. Complete the Temperature Excursion Report (Form SCCS-F-016) within 24 hours.

6.3 **Wet Stock**

If product is received wet, or shows evidence of thawing (e.g., carton collapse, staining, or ice crystal formation on the product surface), the product shall be quarantined and assessed by the Quality & Compliance Manager before it is accepted into stock.

**7. STORAGE**

7.1 **Stock Rotation**

All temperature-controlled product shall be stored in accordance with the first-in, first-out (FIFO) principle unless otherwise specified by the customer or the product label. Stock that is received with a shorter remaining shelf life than existing stock shall be placed in front of existing stock.

7.2 **Pallet Placement**

- Pallets shall be placed a minimum of 100 mm away from cold room walls and a minimum of 200 mm below ceiling-mounted evaporator units.
- Pallets shall not be placed on the floor directly beneath evaporator units or air vents.
- Pallets shall not obstruct emergency exits, fire extinguishers, or temperature monitoring sensors.
- A minimum aisle width of 1.2 metres shall be maintained between pallet racks.

7.3 **Storage of Damaged or Leaking Product**

Product that is damaged or leaking shall be removed from the cold room immediately and placed in the designated damaged goods area. The Shift Supervisor shall be notified so that the damage can be assessed and documented.

**8. DISPATCH**

8.1 **Staging**

Product to be dispatched shall be moved from the cold room to the Chilled Dispatch Staging Bay no more than 30 minutes prior to the scheduled loading time. Product shall not be staged in an unrefrigerated area.

8.2 **Loading**

- The loading dock door shall be opened only when the transport vehicle is backed into the dock and the dock seal is engaged.
- The loading dock door shall be closed when loading is interrupted for more than 5 minutes.
- The transport vehicle's refrigeration unit shall be running and verified to be at the correct temperature before loading commences.

**11. EQUIPMENT MAINTENANCE**

11.1 **Preventative Maintenance**

All refrigeration units, temperature monitoring equipment, and dock seals shall be maintained in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendations and the Preventative Maintenance Schedule (Form M-101).

11.2 **Calibration**

Temperature monitoring equipment shall be calibrated annually or when the unit has been dropped, damaged, or suspected of being inaccurate. Calibration shall be traceable to a national standard.

11.3 **Breakdowns**

In the event of a refrigeration breakdown, the Shift Supervisor shall be notified immediately. The following steps shall be taken:

1. Move product to an alternative temperature-controlled area where possible.
2. Monitor the temperature of the affected area closely.
3. If the breakdown is not resolved within 2 hours, the Quality & Compliance Manager shall be notified.
4. A record of the breakdown and the actions taken shall be made on the Equipment Breakdown Log (Form M-102).

**12. AUDITS AND REVIEW**

12.1 **Internal Audits**

Internal audits of this procedure shall be conducted at least annually by the Quality & Compliance team. The audit shall cover compliance with the requirements of this procedure and the effectiveness of the controls in place.

12.2 **Corrective Actions**

Any non-conformances identified during an audit shall be recorded and corrective actions shall be implemented. The corrective actions shall be reviewed at the next scheduled audit.

14 **Training Requirements**

14.1 **General**

All personnel who handle, receive, or dispatch temperature-controlled product shall complete the training requirements set out in this section before they are permitted to work without direct supervision. Training records shall be maintained by the Training Coordinator and made available to the Quality & Compliance Manager on request.

Training is competency based. Personnel must demonstrate they can perform each task correctly before sign-off is recorded. A training record that is not signed by both the trainee and the assessor is not valid.

14.2 **Induction Training**

New starters shall complete the following modules as part of their induction, before commencing work in the cold chain area:

- Introduction to cold chain principles (including the importance of maintaining temperature integrity)
- Reading and understanding temperature logs
- Use of the temperature monitoring system (both fixed sensors and handheld probes)
- Correct use of thermal blankets and insulated pallet covers
- Dock seal operation and inspection
- Emergency procedures for temperature excursions
- Manual handling and cold room safety (including the buddy system for work in freezer areas)

Induction training is a one-off requirement. It does not need to be repeated if the employee transfers between shifts, provided there is no gap in service of more than 12 months.

14.3 **Role-Specific Training**

The following roles require additional training beyond the induction modules:

| Role | Additional Training Required |
|------|------------------------------|
| Forklift operators | Cold room forklift operation, including use of the heated cab and battery management in low temperatures |
| Receiving clerks | Incoming goods inspection, including probe placement and rejection criteria |
| Dispatch clerks | Load verification, pallet stabilisation, and outbound temperature checks |
| Shift supervisors | All of the above, plus temperature excursion response and escalation |
| Maintenance staff | Calibration checks of probes and sensors, and fault reporting |

14.4 **Annual Refresher**

All personnel who work in the cold chain area shall complete an annual refresher. The refresher shall cover:

- Any changes to this procedure since the previous training
- A practical demonstration of probe use and temperature logging
- A review of any temperature excursions or near misses that occurred in the past 12 months
- A short written assessment (pass mark 80%)

The refresher shall be completed no later than 12 months after the previous training date. Failure to complete the refresher will result in the employee being placed on supervised duties until training is completed.

14.5 **Training Records**

Training records shall include:

- Employee name and employee ID
- Date of training
- Modules completed
- Name and signature of the assessor
- Result of any written assessment
- Date of next refresher due

Training records shall be kept for a minimum of 3 years after the employee leaves the company.

15 **Compliance Monitoring**

15.1 **Routine Checks**

The following checks shall be completed on a routine basis. Results shall be recorded on the relevant form.

| Check | Frequency | Form | Responsible |
|-------|-----------|------|-------------|
| Temperature log review (all cold rooms) | Daily | F-201 | Shift supervisor |
| Probe calibration check | Weekly | F-202 | Maintenance |
| Dock seal inspection | Weekly | F-203 | Shift supervisor |
| Cold room door operation | Weekly | F-204 | Maintenance |
| Stock rotation check (FEFO) | Monthly | F-205 | Inventory controller |
| Pallet condition check | Monthly | F-206 | Shift supervisor |

15.2 **Temperature Log Review**

The shift supervisor shall review all temperature logs at the start of each shift. The review shall confirm:

- All readings are within the acceptable range for the relevant cold room
- Any readings outside the acceptable range have been flagged and investigated
- The probe used for each reading was calibrated and in date
